subject_line: The swap keeping your sugar cravings alive
opening: Happy Sunday, friend. This week's community was on fire debating sweet swaps, lab results, and what to say when people tell you you've lost too much. We've got a lot to get into, and at least one answer in here might surprise you.

hero.title: What Actually Kills Sugar Cravings on Carnivore
hero.teaser: Over 378 people jumped into the comments this week arguing about the best sweet swap on carnivore. Dark chocolate, berries, keto desserts, you name it, someone defended it. But Sarah's answer isn't about finding a better swap. It's about why the swap itself might be the thing keeping you stuck in the craving loop in the first place.
hero.cta: Read before your next craving hits

supporting.title: High Ferritin on Carnivore: Should You Worry?
supporting.teaser: Your doctor circled a number on your labs and mentioned the beef, but Sarah says that flagged ferritin reading might not mean what your doctor thinks it means.

supporting.title: When People Say You Look Too Thin
supporting.teaser: You did the work, hit your goal, and now the people closest to you are worried, so Chloe gets honest about where those comments really come from.

supporting.title: Carnivore Weight Loss Timeline After 50
supporting.teaser: Month one feels like progress, but Sarah says month two is where everything changes, and most people over 50 don't expect what comes next.

community_pulse.question: I've always been a sweets person and I'm brand new to carnivore. Berries and dark chocolate aren't cutting it. What actually works for cravings?
community_pulse.answer: This one came up a lot this week, and it connects directly to Sarah's hero piece above. Many people find that sweet swaps keep the craving alive rather than quieting it. The fix isn't a better substitute, and Sarah breaks down exactly why in 'What Actually Kills Sugar Cravings on Carnivore.'

community_pulse.question: I skipped the rice at a work lunch and only ate the chicken, and suddenly everyone wanted to know why I eat that way. How do you handle the attention?
community_pulse.answer: You're not alone. Community members report this kind of lunch-table moment happens constantly, especially in the first few months. A short, confident answer like 'I just feel better eating this way' tends to close the conversation faster than a full explanation ever does.

community_pulse.question: My therapist told me I should never do keto because of my history with binge eating. Has anyone else been told that by a professional?
community_pulse.answer: That's a hard thing to hear, especially when you're trying to make real changes. Many people with similar histories have found that working with a doctor or dietitian alongside their therapist, rather than choosing one or the other, opened more doors. It's worth getting more than one professional opinion before you decide.

try_this_week: Notice what you reach for when a craving hits. This week, before you grab a sweet swap, pause for 60 seconds and ask whether you're actually hungry or just riding out a signal. Many people find the craving passes on its own with a glass of water and a small portion of protein. That single habit shift is what Sarah's article is really about.
looking_ahead: Next week we're looking at something most carnivores don't check until it's already a problem, and once you know what to watch for, you won't be able to unsee it.
